Dear Pamela, Carlo, and the OSI community,
Thank you for your detailed feedback. As a 9-year-old developer, I am very excited to discuss the Milenium License 1.0 with you.
Regarding your comments:

  1.
The Name: The name "Milenium" is a deliberate branding choice for my project and is not a misspelling.
  2.
Section 4 (Proprietary Use): My intention was not to prohibit commercial use but to prevent the software from being turned into closed-source software. I understand that Section 3 (Copyleft) already covers this. I will revise or remove Section 4 to ensure it complies with OSD 6.
  3.
Section 6 (Lineage and Copyright): I understand the concerns about reusability. I will modify this section so that other developers can use the license for their own projects while still maintaining a way to track the original software's lineage.
  4.
Language Clarity: I will work on making the legal language more precise, including the definitions of "persons" and "public disclosure" as suggested.

I will prepare Milenium License 1.1 based on these professional insights.
Best regards, Yiğit Hamza Founder, Radio Tech's / Create The Developers
I really did my best using all the open-source resources I could find, but I’m still working on improving my skills. I’m really hoping to be accepted. I’m a 9-year-old developer.

A few comments on this submission:

1. The name "Milenium" is spelled inconsistently throughout the license. 
If the license is going to use an incorrect spelling for the title of 
this license, it ought to at least be consistent.

2. As Kevin Fleming previously pointed out, this submission has not 
followed the process of answering the questions about this license, and 
this re-submission has not corrected that:

https://opensource.org/licenses/review-process

3. The License Grant section is very oddly worded, as the statements 
after the term "granted" are not grants, and the purported grants 
precede the "grant." If you're going to draft something based on MIT, 
you really ought to follow the way MIT formulates, e.g., the grant.

4. "Publicly accessible" is undefined.

5. the "Registered License Restriction" clause is confusingly written 
(as is the use of the word "Registered") as it seems to indicate that 
"the same freedoms" are closed-source. Also, what is meant by 
"accessible" in this clause is undefined, and likely violates Freedom 
Zero (which *I* personally believe is inherent in the OSD). Same problem 
is in Sec 7.

6.  Generally, is license is poorly written and has many ambiguities. 
Which is why answering all questions required by the approval process is 
needed.
